unilateral_approvals.title: Unilateral approvals (critical disagreement)
unilateral_approvals.definition: Complete relationship ratings: one rater approves all four substantive criteria and the other rejects at least one.

shared_rejection_diagnosis_divergence.title: Different diagnoses in shared rejections
shared_rejection_diagnosis_divergence.definition: Both reject the relationship, but their full sets of rejected criteria differ. Includes partial overlap and no shared reason.

competing_rdf_relations.title: Competing relations in final RDF graphs
competing_rdf_relations.definition: One case per Identifier and unordered endpoint pair present in both final graphs, with different predicate/direction triple sets. All alternatives are retained; no one-to-one edit is assumed.

unilateral_unresolved_entities.title: Unilateral explicitly unresolved entity corrections
unilateral_unresolved_entities.definition: A relationship has an explicit unresolved-entity correction marker from exactly one rater. Marker absence is unknown, not proof of successful resolution.

a1.source_text: A lake is often a naturally occurring, relatively large and fixed body of water on or near the Earth's surface. It is localized in a basin or interconnected basins surrounded by dry land. A pond is a small, still, land-based body of water formed by pooling inside a depression, either naturally or artificially. A pond is smaller than a lake and there are no official criteria distinguishing the two, although defining a pond to be less than 5 hectares in area, less than 5 metres in depth and with less than 30% of its area covered by emergent vegetation helps in distinguishing the ecology of ponds from those of lakes and wetlands.
